problem: LLM-based Minecraft agents (AutoGPT, Voyager) are inefficient and struggle to integrate multimodal input with autonomous decision-making, and separate agent components (vision, skills, critic, memory, multi-agent planning) have not been built into one coherent system.
motivation: Real-world embodied agents are costly and uncontrollable to train and deploy, so Minecraft serves as a controllable open-world testbed. The paper builds an agent step by step, from an LLM to a vision-augmented model, then a Critic+memory system, a hierarchical multi-agent system, and finally a distilled single model.
key_idea: Build a Minecraft agent incrementally: LLM plus vision encoder and skill-code base (STEVE-1), then hierarchical multi-agent planning (STEVE-1.5), then distillation of the whole system into a single model (STEVE-2).
insight: The paper reports gains from adding vision, hierarchical multi-agent cooperation and distillation, but this short workshop summary has no ablations isolating each stage. The evidence is only cross-method comparison tables, so the insight is limited to the claim that hierarchical structure plus distillation beats prior LLM agents on navigation and creation.
method: STEVE-21K dataset: 600 vision-environment pairs, 20,000 QA pairs and 210 skill-code pairs used to train the multimodal LLM.
STEVE-1: fine-tuned STEVE-13B LLM with a vision unit and an action/skill code base, run through MineDojo and Mineflayer APIs.
STEVE-2 vision: incorporates LLaVA-style visual models for stronger multimodal processing.
Hierarchical multi-agent system (STEVE-1.5): centralized planning with decentralized execution for navigation and creation tasks.
Critic and memory: added to turn the base agent into a complex system.
Hierarchical knowledge distillation (STEVE-2): distills the agent system into a single model, with an extra expert to enhance the teacher.
Creation module: finetuned VQ-VAE for 3D occupancy generation in building tasks.

setting.backbone: STEVE-13B (fine-tuned LLM) with LLaVA-style vision encoder; distilled single model for STEVE-2
setting.training_data: STEVE-21K: 600 vision-environment pairs, 20,000 QA pairs, 210 skill-code pairs
setting.observation: Minecraft egocentric visual input plus game state via APIs

numbers_note: The paper reports only Minecraft benchmarks (knowledge QA, tech tree, goal search, map exploration, material collection, building FID), which are not in the canonical navigation benchmark list, and it has no standard navigation metrics such as SR/SPL. Nothing is extracted for the numbers field.
results: STEVE-2 reaches 91% goal-search success against 64% for Voyager and STEVE-1, and explores 1493 map areas against 755 for Voyager. It reaches 99% material collection against Voyager's 72%, and FID 21.12 against 68.32 for Creative Agents. STEVE-1 needs 33 iterations on tech tree mastery against 35 for Voyager and 107 for AutoGPT.
limitations: Only a brief workshop summary with no ablations, training details or full protocol descriptions.
Evaluated only in Minecraft with no real-world experiments, and some claimed multipliers (e.g. 5.5x, 19x) are not clearly derivable from the tables.
